19009.d:
Abstract, distorted compositions using symbols from the original IBM VGA codepage 437 character set. The symbols were created in code as bitmaps, scaled, and then drawn onto the canvas. The shading is based on the characters and sets from ANSI and ASCII art styles. 

There are 4 main types of outputs:
- Abstracts, 50%
- Random characters, 25%
- One of 16 preset character layouts, 25%
- One of 16 custom symbol PFP styles that will be 10% of the total outputs

For abstracts, there are several main styles created from layering different base shapes: circles, filled circles, rectangles, flow field lines, and rain-like streaks.

Color combinations include monochromatic, green or amber, dark mode, and multicolor.

Press 's' to save the image. The size is 2318x3000px, and for PFPs, the size is 3000x3000px.

Wildebeest also called gnu (/njuː/ NEW or /nuː/ NOO),[5][6][7] are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa. They belong to the family Bovidae, which includes true antelopes, cattle, goats, sheep, and other even-toed horned ungulates. There are two species of wildebeest: the black wildebeest or white-tailed gnu (C. gnou), and the blue wildebeest or brindled gnu (C. taurinus).

Fossil records suggest these two species diverged about one million years ago, resulting in a northern and a southern species. The blue wildebeest remained in its original range and changed very little from the ancestral species, while the black wildebeest changed more as adaptation to its open grassland habitat in the south. The most obvious ways of telling the two species apart are the differences in their colouring and in the way their horns are oriented  -- Wikipedia --

The genesis of this collection are ... good old multiplication tables we all learned back in our days in school. 

There is a pretty interesting way to visualize them : 

Say you take a integer n , ( for example 10 ) and want to represent the table of p ( for example 3 ) for all numbers from 1 to n :
 
You display n dots on a circle labelled from 1 to n
then for each table entry trace a line between dot #i and dot # p x i modulo n 
Example :
1 x 3 = 3 ,  connect n°1 and n°3 
2 x 3 = 6 ,  connect n°2 and n°6 
3 x 3 = 9 ,  connect n°3 and n°9 
4 x 3 = 12 = 10+2 ,  connect n°4 and n°2
5 x 3 = 15 =10+5,  connect n°5 and n°5 
6 x 3 = 18 =10+8,  connect n°6 and n°8 
... 

Play this game with big numbers and you end up with beautiful patterns ...
I took these patterns and twisted them in light & shadow ... 

Made with maths, love and p5.js ... 

Totally responsive , open in live view and play with the browser zoom ...

Calculated in full 64-bit on the CPU (not the GPU) for more accurate and detailed images.

A circle is a shape consisting of all points in a plane that are at a given distance from a given point, the centre. Equivalently, it is the curve traced out by a point that moves in a plane so that its distance from a given point is constant. The distance between any point of the circle and the centre is called the radius.

So, I kinda have a thing with language so I tried to find a funny mix of "art" or "genart" and "circle" or "radius".
I ended up using "radius", scrambled it a bit which became "arduis" and replace "ard" with "art". 
The 4 and the S mean like "4 us", hence "4rtiu5" :-)

Project

There aren't much properties that are set, except for "dashed lines" and "blurred gutters". I had a lot of fun making this and was amazed by some really great outputs myself, I hope you guys like it too! :-)
Cheers 🍻

QarcLand is a colorful and wonderful place where every single pixel has its own story to tell. Every day, kids of all ages fly into QarcLand to find the most beautiful pixels they can. Help these kids on their search and you'll soon find that QarcLand will never be the same again!

The origins of Pixel Land are shrouded in mystery, but it is believed that QarcLand was founded by a confused little girl who had just finished reading Alice in Wonderland for the first time. The little girl, who we'll call Alice, took every word of the book literally and was also very fond of playing Adventure. She dreamt about a colorful world where she could run and jump from dot to dot with her friends.

Alice gathered all the pixels she could find and made them her friends. She taught them how to talk and gave them work in QarcLand's shops where they still work today. However, every time Alice went back to visit QarcLand, it had grown even more than when she last left.

A circle is a shape consisting of all points in a plane that are at a given distance from a given point, the centre. Equivalently, it is the curve traced out by a point that moves in a plane so that its distance from a given point is constant. The distance between any point of the circle and the centre is called the radius.

Name

So, I kinda have a thing with language so I tried to find a funny mix of "art" or "genart" and "circle" or "radius".
I ended up using "radius", scrambled it a bit which became "arduis" and replace "ard" with "art". 
The 4 and the S mean like "4 us", hence "4rtiu5" :-)

Project

There aren't much properties that are set, except for "dashed lines" and "blurred gutters". I had a lot of fun making this and was amazed by some really great outputs myself, I hope you guys like it too! :-)
Cheers 🍻

I had a wonderful childhood. I grew up near a big lake, in a house with a huge garden. You could get lost for the whole day, building houses on trees, collecting flowers and stones or stealing food from the vegetable garden. Having a brother of the same age made things even better, endless adventures with somebody saving you every time you are too dumb to realize you are walking into troubles.

We enjoyed the summers with the hot days, the fireflies and the nights full of falling stars. The winters with the snow, the stalactites and our box turtle disappearing for months to then reappear in the spring (Until she did not).

At the same time, taking care of the garden was a big responsibility, affecting our family life in many ways. Numerous times, I felt like the efforts we were putting in to keep it in order were never enough and nature was always faster in restoring her point of view. A struggle that affects us humans since we started to bend nature at our will, thousands of years ago.

In my gardens, I tried to capture this struggle, this constant fight to shape nature at our will.
However, I also tried to represent the beauty that can be found in both savage and human shaped nature, if shaped with love and respect.

I dedicate this project to my grandfather, who gave us a garden.
I am sure he would have loved it.

19093.d:
We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We should move the world to protect animals.

------------------

Bears are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae. They are classified as caniforms, or doglike carnivorans. Although only eight species of bears are extant, they are widespread, appearing in a wide variety of habitats throughout the Northern Hemisphere and partially in the Southern Hemisphere. Bears are found on the continents of North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Common characteristics of modern bears include large bodies with stocky legs, long snouts, small rounded ears, shaggy hair, plantigrade paws with five nonretractile claws, and short tails.

While the polar bear is mostly carnivorous, and the giant panda feeds almost entirely on bamboo, the remaining six species are omnivorous with varied diets. With the exception of courting individuals and mothers with their young, bears are typically solitary animals. They may be diurnal or nocturnal and have an excellent sense of smell. Despite their heavy build and awkward gait, they are adept runners, climbers, and swimmers. Bears use shelters, such as caves and logs, as their dens; most species occupy their dens during the winter for a long period of hibernation, up to 100 days.

19098.d:
Stippled Sketch is an experimental attempt to imitate the result of sitting down and mindlessly finding form on the page. The process of pressing the pen to paper in a rhythmic, repeated pattern can be a form of meditation, much like doodling. 

The form at the center of the sketch can sometimes take a clear and recognizable shape, but it can also appear meandering and meaningless at times. Some forms appear more often than others (such as a clover and circle), but the equation at the core of the algorithm has surprised me quite a few times with unique and unusual shapes, even after reviewing thousands of previews. 

I like to think of this collection as a reflection of a time in my life when I wanted to say so much—and I could put the pen to the paper, but I knew that no words would have any effect, so I sketched to focus my attention on something else instead. 

— — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — 
Special thanks to Laurent Houdard and Lisa Orth for helping with a few technical aspects.

"Totems are objects that represent a group of people, or concept."

For this piece I combined both programmatic generative concepts with organic marks. I focused previous generative projects on animation and interactivity. With Totems I focused more on creating pleasing and balanced compositions regardless of generated characteristics.

---

Totems represents my continued search to discover a type of generative work that I find both pleasing to create and collect. One day once I settle on a particular genre or medium of work, these works will be seen as those that contributed to me "finding myself" or "finding my style".

---

Note that the preview capture requires GPU instancing, so capture may take a couple moments. The rough edges were not rendering without GPU instancing.

A whiff of pattern begins to emerge. Out of disarray comes the familiar pulsation of an ordered signal. The sense of regularity strengthens and we feel it swelling towards a singularity. Heeere weeee goooo… BAM! Then off again marching back into chaos to repeat the cycle.

Proposed by cognitive scientist Douglas Hofstadter in his 1979 book “Gödel, Escher, Bach”, and further developed in his 2007 book “I Am a Strange Loop”, “Strange Loops” are Hofstadter’s attempt at explaining the mechanisms that give rise to the sensation of “I” - through hierarchical, self-referential, and at times seemingly paradoxical feedback-loops of abstraction and causality. 

—

“Who shoves whom around in the tangled megaganglion that is your brain, and who shoves whom around in ‘this teetering bulb of dread and dream’ that is mine?”

“Do dreads and dreams, hopes and griefs, ideas and beliefs, interests and doubts, infatuations and envies, memories and ambitions, bouts of nostalgia and floods of empathy, flashes of guilt and sparks of genius, play any role in the world of physical objects? Do such pure abstractions have causal powers? Can they shove massive things around, or are they just impotent fictions?” 

"In the end, we are self-perceiving, self-inventing, locked-in mirages that are little miracles of self-reference. [...] Poised midway between the unvisualizable cosmic vastness of curved spacetime and the dubious, shadowy flickerings of charged quanta, we human beings, more like rainbows and mirages than like raindrops or boulders, are unpredictable self-writing poems — vague, metaphorical, ambiguous, and sometimes exceedingly beautiful.”

- Douglas Hofstadter, “I Am a Strange Loop”, 2007

We are not the only inhabitants of the earth,

The earth does not belong only to humans

From the seas to the deserts,animals face the ongoing threat of cruelty and abuse. Bears are captured and forced to fight dogs. Marine mammals, such as whales and dolphins, get trapped in discarded fishing gear. Wild animals are traded as exotic pets.

We should end the needless suffering of animals.
We should influence decision makers to put animals on the global agenda.
We should help the world see how important animals are to all of us.
We inspire people to change animals’ lives for the better.
We should move the world to protect animals.

------------------

Bulls are much more muscular than cows, with thicker bones, larger feet, a very muscular neck, and a large, bony head with protective ridges over the eyes. These features assist bulls in fighting for domination over a herd, giving the winner superior access to cows for reproduction.[4] The hair is generally shorter on the body, but the neck and head often have a "mane" of curlier, wooly hair. Bulls are usually about the same height as cows or a little taller, but because of the additional muscle and bone mass, they often weigh far more. Most of the time, a bull has a hump on his shoulders.[5]

In horned cattle, the horns of bulls tend to be thicker and somewhat shorter than those of cows,[6] and in many breeds, they curve outwards in a flat arc rather than upwards in a lyre shape. It is not true, as is commonly believed, that bulls have horns and cows do not: the presence of horns depends on the breed, or in horned breeds on whether the horns have been disbudded. (It is true, however, that in many breeds of sheep only the males have horns.) Cattle that naturally do not have horns are referred to as polled, or muleys.[7]

Castrated male cattle are physically similar to females in build and horn shape, although if allowed to reach maturity, they may be considerably taller than either bulls or cows, with heavily muscled shoulders and necks -- Wikipedia --

========
Concept
========
Humanists live in a world built on human bones.
The fuel of humanism is human sacrifices.

Eating flesh is natural for animals.
But humans are eating  life energy, results of work, time  of other humans.

Social status is in general about how many humans you personally can devour.
Personal freedom in general about how not to be eaten by other humans.

Sweet promises, beautiful concepts, inspiring ideas - basically ways to put  the victim on the skewer.

Humanism today is an attempt to inject anesthesia into the basic process of eating others.
Slavery must be gentle and invisible.
Weapons must be lethal and not cause suffering.
People should be polite and tolerant.
You must not feel that your blood is being sucked out.

If the victim does not feel the pain and does not scream: is the victim a plant? Is predator a vegan?

Is it better to you feel pain or inject anesthesia?
Anesthesia today is not only drugs, but entertainment.

Are you enjoy of eating others?
So check if you are on a skewer and how roasted you are.

==============
Technical Details
==============
Mangal size calculating depending on humans amount (min=5; max=111) and skewer parameters.

You can roast the bodies from different sides using the control buttons.
The bodies are divided into sectors that absorb thermal energy differently depending on the angle of rotation.
The amount of absorbed energy determines the degree of roasting.
The camera is focused on the active skewer, to select another one, press the button or select from the list.

Press the left mouse button to rotate the point of view.
Hold down the right mouse button to move the point of view.

Pastellhood is a generative artwork made up of pastel hues, triangles, circles and rectangles in a grid with a smooth shadow giving the observer the feeling of depth. The pastel hues give the artwork a soft and calming feeling, while the geometric shapes add an element of interest and intrigue. The grid-like structure of the artwork helps to create a sense of balance and order.

When looking at this piece, the observer can feel a sense of calm and serenity while these soft colors and shapes help to create a peaceful and relaxing atmosphere.

Curiosity: Pastel colors have been shown to have a calming effect on people. They are often used in hospitals and waiting rooms because they create a sense of serenity. The soft colors are soothing and can help to lower blood pressure and heart rate.

The simplicity is always an option in my personal projects because it can allow the viewer to focus on the main elements of the piece and appreciate them more. Additionally, it can make the artwork more accessible to a wider audience.

Hope you enjoy!

I surrender to the moment, to the security check. My luggage is what I take with me on my travels. Life is a pilgrimage. It's an endless journey from birth to grave. I bring the memories, the fading, convoluted memories, refractions, reflections, emotions, and tremulous doubts and anxiety.

Security screening at an airport is a necessary but cold and impersonal experience. I surrender my luggage and myself to the scrutiny of a stranger who knows nothing about me and cares even less. They are focused on following the rules and ensuring the safety of others and not on passing judgment on the contents of my life. In the face of their anonymity, I can't help but feel desolate and secluded. 

The chaos of the world around me feels more pronounced in this moment of stillness, and I can't help but feel a sense of anxiety and doubt.

19223.d:
This is the sixth in series of works where we pay homage to Ken Knowlton, scientist and computer graphic pioneer and artist who passed on June 16, 2022. Ken Knowlton developed the famous EXPLOR language, (Explicit 2-D Patterns, Local Operations, and Randomness) while at Bell Labs. He published a paper describing it in 1975 entitled: MINI-EXPLOR, A FORTRAN-Coded Version of the EXPLOR Language for Mini (and larger) Computers. (https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/988049.988052)

I continue to explore the capabilities of EXPLOR. After using it for awhile I realize that it is truly a return to the past where the medium, the language and the machine, were truly primitive. But hey, back then you worked with what you had. That’s what it was like being a pioneer.

For this piece I used an EXPLOR block as a tile. My Boxes algorithm (used in my 2 previous offerings) rotates and translates a tile relative to the distance that tile is to the center of a tessellation, two versions: either more or less. While I cannot rotate a block in EXPLOR I can translate it. In place of rotation I use a relative distance computation to control both  displacement and the percentage rule in EXPLOR’s COMBN function causing the tile to translate and seemingly fragment relative to its position in the array. 

I am amazed by the quality and richness of the images that are generated by this piece especially employing EXPLOR’s limited four color palette. I hope you enjoy them as well.

We continue to honor the passing of Ken Knowlton with this NFT series. Here is an opportunity to collect an example image from the famous program he authored now updated by Scussel and Kolomyjec. A true piece of Computer Graphic Art history with a modern twist.

Solid Line is made of square tiles with predefined patterns, disposed randomly, and on top of which is drawn a line. By isolating the colors, this line creates a new structure of seemingly interlaced shapes.

There are three possible level of details, and a rare "Outline" feature that will render only the line layer.

SVG generated with JavaScript.

The SVG can be saved by pressing "s" on the full-screen view.
A PNG version can be exported by pressing "e" on the full-screen view.

By default the dimensions of the export are 6000×8000.
These dimensions can be changed by adding, for example, ?w=12000 to the full-screen page URL, where w is the desired width. Then press "e" to export at this size.

19237.d:
"Liaisons dangereuses" is a creative exploration of implausible relations between figurative art and poetry. Our AI poet learned on the basis of texts about artists and their work. It memorized all subtleties of a language designed to describe visual emotions and artworks. This language is the tool for creating countless poems about artistic concepts, which range from techniques to materials to artists, etc. But the link is two-sided: if the poet is fed by art language, the concepts expressed by poems do, in turn, influence the appearance of the artwork. Color palettes, pattern types and the flow of the graphic composition are indeed determined by the semantics of the poem.
In each minting, the poet will produce either a short poem (a iambic 5-7-5 haiku  or a iambic cinquain according to Adelaide Crapsey style) or a single verse (either an alexandrine, or a iambic pentameter or an anapestic tetrameter). There are 625 artistic concepts that can trigger a poem, and each concept can generate countless different semantically coherent poems. The poet is completely "unchained": contents might be peaceful harmonic assertions as well as embarrassing, politically incorrect claims, but always avoiding inappropriate language.

You can save to file the image by pressing the "s" key.

I have been exploring the medium of print for years. Mixing etching, silk-screening, offset, photocopy, risography, drawing and painting to design and craft experimental art books.From the day digital, which had always fascinated me, took over my publishing practice, I always liked to create bridges between these two worlds.

The Living Books is part of this series of hybrid and experimental works where paper and digital resonate.

This issue #2 is made of 64 pages that will be minted by collectors. A book will eventually be printed and the pages will follow the mint order. Each page exists in a cover version (c) and a xerox version (x).

Controls :

• Click to dive into each frame.
• Press C to toggle cover mode.
• Press X to toggle xerox mode.
• Press 1, 2, 3, or 4 to make a capture and download a PNG with a resolution of x1, x2, x3 or x4.

The output is and animation, with a still image for the ipfs data.

I studied figure painting in undergrad and grad-school, and I love the way paint strokes push and pull, and play with the composition. My paintings are about the body and identity and just a note, these maybe considered nsfw for some. hit me up :) thanks for looking at my art!

19246.d:
Artwork.
Anchored in a not-so-binary world, the pare1d0scope generates unique patterns of 4-bit squares by applying a generative mix of color palettes, symmetry, ordering, subdividing, and diagonals adjustments.

Geometry.
The algorithm generates a sequence of the 2^4 possible 4-bits squares, adjusts inner diagonals, then draws them on a defined size canvas after applying specific color panels. Symmetry, ordering, and simpler black-and-white palets produce rarer iterations.

Shortcuts: [click] Adjust diagonals of selected 4-bit square iteration, [1-4] Adjust diagonals for all squares, [p] Print png.

Collaboration.
This project is a collaboration between sha22.art and Antonino.
